Rules / Modernization

SK1033 Use TryGetValue or TryAdd instead of ContainsKey and a second lookup

ContainsKey followed by the indexer, or by Add, hashes the key twice to do one thing.

CategoryModernization
Default severitysuggestion
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, safe
Language version floorC# 7.0
Since1.2

Why

if (map.ContainsKey(key)) { var value = map[key]; … } computes the hash, walks the bucket, throws the result away and does all of it again. TryGetValue does it once, and TryAdd is the same saving for the insert. It is filed as modernization rather than performance because it reads as a style preference and is not one: in a loop it is half the lookups, and the shorter form is also the one that cannot go stale between the two statements.

Example

Instead of:

if (map.ContainsKey(key)) {
    var handler = map[key];
    handler.Run();
}

if (!seen.ContainsKey(id)) {
    seen[id] = name;
}

Write:

if (map.TryGetValue(key, out var handler)) {
    handler.Run();
}

seen.TryAdd(id, name);

When it does not fire

None known, and one of the two shapes was measured wrong before it shipped. if (!d.ContainsKey(k)) d[k] = Build(); calls Build() only when the key is absent; d.TryAdd(k, Build()) calls it every time, because C# evaluates arguments before the call, and discards the result when the key was present. On Vixen that was mesh.AddPosition(…), which mutates the mesh, and edited.ToMeshData(…), which builds one — a behaviour change and an allocation added to the common path. So the written value must itself be a plain name or a literal, something already computed. Beyond that: two shapes only, because they are the two where the rewrite is provable — a ContainsKey test whose block opens by reading the same key from the same receiver, and a negated test whose whole body writes that key once. The receiver must be Dictionary<K, V> exactly, since TryAdd is not on IDictionary<K, V> and on a ConcurrentDictionary the ContainsKey/indexer pair is a race whose shape the rewrite would change rather than a redundancy it removes. Receiver and key must be plain names or literals, since both are evaluated once instead of twice. It is silent on an if with an else; on an explicitly typed declaration whose type is not the dictionary's value type, because out object v does not compile; where the name would collide with another local scope of the member; and inside an expression tree.
